proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(\mu_x=\sum_{r\in B^2}\nu_{(x,r)}\).  First suppose that \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\), and define \(\nu\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}response\text{-}measures}\).  This definition uses the product of the two feedback-coordinate marginals only as a coupling that constructs a joint response type; it does not assert stochastic independence of two jointly observed counterfactual responses.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}initial\text{-}kernel}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}feedback\text{-}kernel}\), every \(\nu_s\) is nonnegative and
\[
 \sum_{x\in B}\sum_{r_0,r_1\in B}d\nu_{(x,r_0,r_1)}
 =\sum_{x\in B}h_x
   \left(\sum_{r_0\in B}g_{x0}(r_0,\cdot)\right)
   \left(\sum_{r_1\in B}g_{x1}(r_1,\cdot)\right)d\mu
 =d\mu.
\]
Thus \(\sum_s\nu_s\) is a probability measure by \(\mathrm{ass{:}base\text{-}law}\).  For fixed \((x,y,z,w)\), summation over the response coordinate not selected by \(y\) gives
\[
 \sum_{r:r_y=z}d\nu_{(x,r)}
 =h_xg_{xy}(z,\cdot)
   \sum_{r_{1-y}\in B}g_{x,1-y}(r_{1-y},\cdot)d\mu
 =h_xg_{xy}(z,\cdot)d\mu. \tag{1}
\]
The model-generated path law uses the two response probabilities in \(\mathrm{ass{:}logit\text{-}response}\).  Multiplying (1) by \(p_x(y,\cdot)p_z(w,\cdot)\) and integrating proves
\[
 P(x,y,z,w)=\sum_{r:r_y=z}\int p_x(y,u)p_z(w,u)d\nu_{(x,r)}(u).
\]
Likewise, because \(\sum_s d\nu_s=d\mu\),
\[
 \sum_s\int\frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}d\nu_s(u)
 =\int\frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}d\mu(u)=\Delta.
\]

Conversely, suppose the eight finite nonnegative measures satisfy the two displayed equations in the statement and that \(\mu=\sum_s\nu_s\) is a probability measure.  For \(x,y,z\in B\), define
\[
 \mu_x=\sum_{r\in B^2}\nu_{(x,r)},
 \qquad
 \lambda_{xyz}=\sum_{r:r_y=z}\nu_{(x,r)}.
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_x\mu_x=\mu,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{xy0}+\lambda_{xy1}=\mu_x,
 \qquad
 \sum_{x,y,z}\frac12\lambda_{xyz}=\mu. \tag{2}
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}radon\text{-}nikodym\text{-}finite\text{-}family}\) first to \((\mu_x)_{x\in B}\) and then to \((\lambda_{xyz}/2)_{x,y,z\in B}\).  After multiplying the derivatives in the second application by two, there are simultaneously measurable functions
\[
 h_x=\frac{d\mu_x}{d\mu},
 \qquad
 k_{xyz}=\frac{d\lambda_{xyz}}{d\mu}
\]
with \(h_x\ge0\), \(k_{xyz}\ge0\), and \(\sum_xh_x=1\), all \(\mu\)-almost everywhere.  The middle equality in (2) and uniqueness of Radon--Nikodym derivatives imply
\[
 k_{xy0}+k_{xy1}=h_x
 \quad\text{for every }x,y\in B,
 \quad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}. \tag{3}
\]
Because there are finitely many indices, the versions may be fixed on one common full-\(\mu\)-measure set.  Define
\[
 g_{xy}(z,u)=
 \begin{cases}
 k_{xyz}(u)/h_x(u),&h_x(u)>0,\\
 1/2,&h_x(u)=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Division occurs only on \(\{h_x>0\}\).  Measurability follows from measurability of \(h_x\) and \(k_{xyz}\); (3) gives \(g_{xy}(z,\cdot)\ge0\) and \(\sum_zg_{xy}(z,\cdot)=1\) almost everywhere.  On \(\{h_x=0\}\), (3) and nonnegativity give \(k_{xyz}=0\), whereas the displayed fallback itself is a probability vector.  Therefore
\[
 h_xg_{xy}(z,\cdot)d\mu=k_{xyz}d\mu=d\lambda_{xyz}. \tag{4}
\]
The base law, initial kernel, and feedback kernel consequently satisfy \(\mathrm{ass{:}base\text{-}law}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}initial\text{-}kernel}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}feedback\text{-}kernel}\); adjoining the fixed response probabilities gives an element of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\).  By (4), its generated cells are
\[
 \int h_x(u)p_x(y,u)g_{xy}(z,u)p_z(w,u)d\mu(u)
 =\int p_x(y,u)p_z(w,u)d\lambda_{xyz}(u)
 =P(x,y,z,w).
\]
Finally, summing the stipulated APE equation over the same response measures and using \(\mu=\sum_s\nu_s\) gives the model APE \(\Delta\).  This proves both directions and the asserted legal-kernel reconstruction.

Fix \(c>0\).  The restriction \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}observed\text{-}cells}\) places \(P\) in the stated full positive-law domain.  Every division or change of measure below instead uses the explicitly stated facts \(c>0\), \(u>0\), and Radon--Nikodym domination.

Start with a legal weak model.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}response\text{-}measure\text{-}equivalence}\), it yields eight nonnegative joint response measures \(\nu_s\) whose sum is one probability measure.  Since
\[
 D_c(u)=(1+u)^2(1+cu)^2>0
 \quad(c>0, u>0),
\]
define \(d\rho_s=D_c^{-1}d\nu_s\).  For each \(0\le k\le4\), the function \(u^k/D_c(u)\) is bounded on \((0,\infty)\): it has a finite limit as \(u\downarrow0\), and it is of order \(u^{k-4}\) as \(u\to\infty\).  Thus all five moments \(m_{s,k}\) are finite.  Direct cancellation using the definition of \(p\) gives
\[
 D_c(u)p_x(y,u)p_z(w,u)
 =c^{xy+zw}u^{y+w}(1+u)^{x+z}(1+cu)^{2-x-z}
 =A_{xz,yw}(u), \tag{5}
\]
and the definition of the APE integrand gives
\[
 D_c(u)\frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}
 =(c-1)u(1+u)(1+cu)=N_c(u). \tag{6}
\]
The polynomials in (5)--(6) have degree at most four.  Hence the response-measure equations are exactly
\[
 P(x,y,z,w)=\sum_{r:r_y=z}L_{m_{(x,r)}}(A_{xz,yw}),
 \qquad
 \Delta=\sum_{s\in S}L_{m_s}(N_c). \tag{7}
\]
For every type, \(\mathrm{lem{:}open\text{-}stieltjes\text{-}quartic}\) supplies \(a_s,b_s\) such that \(H_s\succeq0\) and \(K_s\succeq0\).  Equations (7) and \(\mathrm{def{:}weak\text{-}lift}\) prove \(\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing\).

Suppose now that the original model is strict.  For every \(s=(x,r_0,r_1)\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}initial}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}feedback}\) imply
\[
 h_x(u)g_{x0}(r_0,u)g_{x1}(r_1,u)>0
 \quad\text{for }\mu\text{-almost every }u.
\]
Consequently every \(\nu_s\), and hence every \(\rho_s\), is mutually absolutely continuous with \(\mu\).  If \(v=(v_0,v_1,v_2)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(q_v(u)=v_0+v_1u+v_2u^2\), then
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}H_sv=\int q_v(u)^2d\rho_s(u).
\]
Mutual absolute continuity makes the null space of this quadratic form identical for every \(s\).  Thus all \(H_s\) have the same range; because a sum of positive-semidefinite matrices has null space equal to the intersection of their null spaces, \(H_\Sigma\) has that same range.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}generalized\text{-}schur\text{-}range}\) with \(A=H_s\) and \(B=H_\Sigma\) produces \(t_s\) such that \(R_s\succeq0\) for every \(s\).  This proves \(\mathcal F_c^+(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing\).

Conversely, let \((m,a,b)\in\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}open\text{-}stieltjes\text{-}quartic}\), for each \(s\) there is a finite nonnegative measure \(\rho_s\) on \((0,\infty)\) with moments \(m_{s,0},\ldots,m_{s,4}\).  Set
\[
 d\nu_s(u)=D_c(u)d\rho_s(u).
\]
This is finite because \(D_c\) is a degree-four polynomial and the moments through degree four are finite.  To find its total mass, sum all sixteen cell equations in (7).  For a fixed \(s=(x,r)\), the restriction \(r_y=z\) selects exactly one \(z\) for each \(y\), and the response probabilities obey \(\sum_w p_{r_y}(w,u)=1\) and \(\sum_y p_x(y,u)=1\).  Equivalently, summing (5) over these indices yields \(D_c\).  Since \(P\in\Delta^{15}\),
\[
 1=\sum_{x,y,z,w}P(x,y,z,w)
  =\sum_{s\in S}L_{m_s}(D_c)
  =\sum_{s\in S}\nu_s((0,\infty)). \tag{8}
\]
Thus the response measures have one probability total.  Identities (5)--(7) show that their path and APE integrals equal exactly \(P\) and \(\Delta\).  The reverse implication in \(\mathrm{lem{:}response\text{-}measure\text{-}equivalence}\) reconstructs one common unconditional law and legal kernels \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\).  Hence \((\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)\).

It remains to verify the strict converse.  Let \((m,a,b,t)\in\mathcal F_c^+(P,\Delta)\).  From \(R_s\succeq0\), \(\mathrm{lem{:}generalized\text{-}schur\text{-}range}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Range}(H_\Sigma)\subseteq\operatorname{Range}(H_s)
 \quad\text{for every }s. \tag{9}
\]
Because \(H_\Sigma-H_s=\sum_{j\ne s}H_j\succeq0\), one has \(\ker(H_\Sigma)\subseteq\ker(H_s)\), and symmetry therefore gives the reverse range inclusion.  The ranges in (9) are equal.  If some \(H_s=0\), (9) forces \(H_\Sigma=0\); positive semidefiniteness then forces every \(H_j=0\).  Since the entries of \(H_j\) comprise \(m_{j,0},\ldots,m_{j,4}\), every moment coordinate is then zero and the right side of (8) is zero, a contradiction.  Thus every \(m_s\ne0\).

All hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}positive\text{-}support}\) now hold.  Choose finite representing measures \(\rho_s\) on one positive-node set \(Q\subset(0,\infty)\), with every \(\rho_s\) assigning strictly positive weight to every \(q\in Q\).  Multiplication by \(D_c(q)>0\) preserves positivity of every type weight for \(\nu_s=D_c\rho_s\).  With \(\mu=\sum_s\nu_s\), define the Radon--Nikodym reconstructions from \(\mathrm{lem{:}response\text{-}measure\text{-}equivalence}\) nodewise.  At each \(q\in Q\),
\[
 h_x(q)=\frac{\sum_{r\in B^2}\nu_{(x,r)}(\{q\})}{\sum_{j\in S}\nu_j(\{q\})}>0,
\]
and, for every \(x,y,z\in B\),
\[
 g_{xy}(z,q)=
 \frac{\sum_{r:r_y=z}\nu_{(x,r)}(\{q\})}{\sum_{r\in B^2}\nu_{(x,r)}(\{q\})}>0.
\]
Both denominators are positive because every type has positive weight at every node.  Since \(\mu\) is concentrated on \(Q\), these inequalities hold \(\mu\)-almost everywhere and establish \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}initial}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}feedback}\).  Therefore the reconstructed model lies in \(\mathcal M_+(c)\), and \((\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_+(P)\).

Finally, \(m\) has \(8\cdot5=40\) coordinates and \((a,b)\) has sixteen, so the weak lift has exactly fifty-six scalar variables, eight \(3\times3\) blocks \(H_s\), and eight \(4\times4\) blocks \(K_s\).  The strict lift adds the eight coordinates of \(t\) and eight \(6\times6\) blocks \(R_s\), for sixty-four variables.  The two-sided constructions prove equality with the independently model-defined fibers, rather than an outer bound.  The cited \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}continuous\text{-}feedback\text{-}program}\) identifies the published continuous-heterogeneity weak program and its support-grid implementation.  The equivalence proved above removes its infinite-dimensional measure quantifier without changing the weak legal models, and the common-support argument does the same for the additional strict legal restriction.  This proves the stated finite-dimensional tightening and completes both equivalences.

prose_updates.tldr: For a two-period binary logit panel with a predetermined binary covariate, continuous unrestricted heterogeneity, and heterogeneity-dependent initial assignment and feedback, the model-generated joint slope--APE fibers equal finite quartic Stieltjes feasibility sets. Eight coupled response-type measures preserve one unconditional heterogeneity law and reconstruct legal sequential kernels without a cross-world independence assumption. The weak certificate has fifty-six variables with eight \(3\times3\) and eight augmented \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; strict almost-everywhere assignment and feedback positivity has sixty-four variables and eight further \(6\times6\) common-range blocks. Downstream results give sharp fixed-slope endpoint programs with separate attainment tests, terminating algebraic membership and projection, exact multinomial whole-set coverage, and pointwise endpoint consistency only at relative-interior attainable laws. Uniform inference at rank-changing boundary laws and joint consistency through \(c=1\) remain open.

project_justification.gap: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham characterize the sharp unrestricted-feedback model by an infinite-dimensional continuous-heterogeneity program and compute with support grids. Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell develop truncated-Stieltjes tools for a different conditional structure, but do not reconstruct a separately unknown heterogeneity-dependent feedback kernel from one unconditional mixing law.
project_justification.niche: At two periods, an artificial product coupling of the two feedback-coordinate marginals creates eight joint response types without asserting cross-world independence. The binary-logit path likelihoods share a positive quartic denominator, so five bounded generalized moments per type suffice; common Hankel range is exactly what upgrades separate open-half-line representability to a shared finite positive-node support with every type weight positive.
project_justification.fill: The note defines weak and strict identified fibers from legal sequential models and proves two-sided maps between those models, eight response-type measures, and finite Stieltjes lifts. The reverse map constructs one unconditional probability law and normalized measurable initial and feedback kernels. The same exact cone supports sharp endpoint and attainment formulas, algebraic decision procedures, conservative exact multinomial set inversion, and fixed-slope relative-interior consistency.

sampling_model.design: Observational two-period binary panel with exact inversion of the sixteen-cell law.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent units drawn from the population law \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: The binary predetermined covariate \(X_t\) is not randomized. Initial assignment and the feedback distribution of \(X_2\) after \((X_1,Y_1)\) may depend arbitrarily on \(u\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell is positive. The weak latent model permits zero assignment or feedback probabilities; the strict latent model requires almost-everywhere positivity, with no numerical lower bound. Observed-cell positivity alone does not imply the strict latent condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cell law is estimated by multinomial frequencies. Whole-set inversion uses simultaneous Clopper--Pearson marginal intervals, while fixed-slope endpoint estimation projects frequencies onto the relevant attainable affine hull.

prose_updates.related_work: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Proposition 1 and Sections 5.1--5.3, provide the sharp continuous-heterogeneity unrestricted-feedback program and its support-grid implementation. The exact-feedback-cone theorem gives a two-sided finite representation of the same weak legal fiber and of the explicitly strengthened strict fiber. Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026), Theorems 3.1--3.2, provide rational-mixture and truncated-Stieltjes ideas, but their model does not contain the separately unknown unrestricted feedback kernel reconstructed here. Curto and Fialkow (1991) and Bayer and Teichmann (2002) provide classical moment and finite-atomic substrate for singular open-half-line faces. Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2026) study feedback-robust moment equalities, while Gu, Russell, and Stringham (2026) use finite latent-cell enumeration for discrete-outcome index models; neither result supplies this continuous-logit legal-kernel equivalence. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) and Pakel and Weidner (2026) motivate, but do not solve, the remaining rank-changing inference problem. Arellano and Carrasco (2003) provide the predetermined-children labor-participation design that can consume the exact bounds.
prose_updates.interpretation: The finite cone is an identifying map for the independently defined causal slope--APE fiber, not a regression estimand or a discretized outer approximation. Weak feasibility permits type measures with different supports. Strict feasibility is stronger: the common-range blocks certify a representation on one positive-node set with every response type receiving positive weight, which is exactly what makes all reconstructed initial and feedback probabilities positive almost everywhere.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The strict common-support proof is existential and does not provide an efficient atom-extraction algorithm. Real quantifier elimination terminates for algebraic inputs but carries no polynomial complexity or numerical-stability guarantee. A closed lifted PSD set can have a nonclosed linear image, so fixed-slope infima and suprema need separate endpoint-attainment tests. Relative-interior convex continuity does not extend automatically to attainable boundary laws, changes of Hankel rank, or the observable-map rank loss at \(c=1\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: The primitive targets are the model-generated weak and strict fibers. The proved contribution is their exact finite-certificate equivalence, including forward joint-response construction, reverse legal-kernel reconstruction, and the common-support certificate required for strict positivity. The note also delivers sharp fixed-slope endpoints with separate inclusion tests, algebraic membership and projection, a direct conservative exact multinomial whole-set inversion, and pointwise endpoint consistency for fixed \(c\) at relative-interior attainable laws. It imposes no support grid, latent density, tail moment, or numerical overlap margin. Boundary-uniform inference, continuity at strictly positive relative-boundary laws, joint consistency through \(c=1\), efficient certified extraction, arbitrary \(T\), restricted feedback dynamics, and multinomial outcomes remain outside the proved scope.

statement_notes.justification: This is the legal-kernel reconstruction step: one family of eight joint response-type measures determines a common base law and compatible measurable initial and feedback kernels.
statement_notes.gap: The published history-density formulation enforces compatibility inside an infinite-dimensional program; it does not give this finite response-type coupling and Radon--Nikodym reconstruction.
statement_notes.consumer: It reduces unrestricted feedback to eight univariate moment problems without adding cross-world independence or changing the weak model class.

statement_notes.justification: The two-sided theorem removes both the support-grid approximation and the latent-law quantifier while preserving the independently defined weak and strict causal fibers.
statement_notes.gap: The closest feedback program remains infinite-dimensional, and the closest truncated-Stieltjes analysis does not provide the separate unrestricted-feedback kernel or the common-support strict-positivity reconstruction.
statement_notes.consumer: The exact finite cone supplies sharp, grid-free slope--APE feasibility and endpoint calculations for the two-wave predetermined-children labor-participation design.
